title: Lydia (Acts 16:11–15)
hookLine: a businesswoman in purple cloth, the first convert in Europe, opens her home
last: IT HATH SEEMED GOOD TO THE HOLY GHOST.

lines: NOT A MAN: A GROUP OF WOMEN.
cards: Paul has just seen a vision in the night: a man of Macedonia, standing and begging, come over and help us. So Paul and his companions sail from Asia to the north of Greece, to Philippi, a Roman colony.
They're expecting a man. On the Sabbath they walk out of the city gate to the riverside, where they think there's a place of prayer. And the people waiting there aren't men at all.
It's a group of women. Paul sits down and starts talking with them.

teach.h: A SELLER OF PURPLE FROM THYATIRA.
teach.b: One of them is named Lydia, and Luke tells us three things about her in one breath. She's from Thyatira, a city back across the sea in Asia.
She's a seller of purple, a costly dyed cloth, so she's a businesswoman, with a household and a house of her own. And she worships God: a Gentile who prays with the Jewish community.

Then the line the whole story turns on, in the Douay-Rheims: "whose heart the Lord opened to attend to those things which were said by Paul." Notice who does the opening. Paul talks; the Lord opens; Lydia listens.
She and her household are baptized, perhaps in that same river.
Then she does something practical: if you judge me faithful to the Lord, she says, come and stay at my house. And Luke adds, she constrained us. She wouldn't take no for an answer.

teach.h: AN OPENED HEART, AN OPENED DOOR.
teach.b: An opened heart becomes an opened door. Her house becomes the church of Philippi: after the jail scene coming tomorrow, Paul goes back to Lydia's house to see the brethren before leaving town.
Years later, Paul writes to the Philippians, thanking them for their partnership from the first day. That church began on a riverbank, with a woman who sold purple cloth and opened her home.

how: Catholics honor Saint Lydia, and many parishes and Catholic homes practice hospitality through welcome ministries, shared meals and hosting prayer groups; in the early Church, believers met in homes like hers.

games.why: she says, if you judge me faithful, come and stay, and won't take no. her house becomes the church in Philippi.

practice: Picture your front door: who has come through it lately, and who hasn't who might be glad to, a neighbor you only wave at, a friend who's been lonely, someone new at work or at church.

It doesn't have to be dinner for twelve; coffee counts, a seat on the porch counts, so picture inviting that one person, simply and insistently, the way Lydia did. If you pray, ask that your heart be opened, like hers.

wordCard.voice: Lydia. The seller of purple from Thyatira, whose heart the Lord opened by a river, and who opened her house to the church. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: seller of purple, a woman dealing in costly dyed cloth. Luke's word for Lydia's trade.
